page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-32 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 8 dedicated physical cores supporting simultaneous multithreading, providing 16 vCPUs at two threads per core. The memory subsystem provides 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB of memory per core.

Operating on the x86_64 architecture, VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-32 contains no integrated local disk storage and includes no GPU accelerators. Workloads running on this instance require external network block storage for operating system files and persistent data retention. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory density provides a balance suited for compute-heavy applications rather than memory-saturated deployments. Dedicated core provisioning ensures predictable execution without hypervisor scheduling contention. The instance profile is suited for continuous integration and deployment pipelines, distributed processing workers, code compilation, and general web application hosting.

It provisions 16 vCPUs derived from 8 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system includes 32.0 GB of memory, which establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block volumes for persistent data needs. Network communication is enabled with one complimentary public IPv4 address. Due to its dedicated processor cores and moderate memory footprint, VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-32 is suited for compute-focused tasks such as batch execution, build systems, background processing queues, and microservice infrastructure.
